correctness.rationale: The 3-e.c. iff unrestricted FO^4 random-graph equivalence follows from explicit four-variable extension axioms and a permanent four-pebble invariant. Every mixed-coordinate triangle forces the rectangle law, which makes the relative row permutations fixed-point-free involutions; their commuting regular group gives the Boolean-group table. Orders 2 and 4 have explicit missing patterns; dimension at least four has an explicit independent-vector triple with no common neighbor. For the sole remaining 8x8 table, check_full.py enumerates every one of 41,664 triples and all 333,312 adjacency patterns; check_translation.py separately confirms 3-e.c. by 3,906 relative ordered anchor pairs. The two programs ran successfully and reproduced the embedded outputs. The displayed singleton witness and translation symmetry establish vertex criticality. The exhaustive finite search proves only the fixed 64-vertex case, and the algebraic reduction proves that this suffices.

originality.rationale: The nearest 2003/2008 affine-plane results concern roughly half the parallel classes (odd q, or q/2 classes in even q). The 2008 order-eight graph has four parallel classes and valency 28; the present graph has exactly three and valency 21. Neither proves that *every* three-coordinate Latin-square graph which is 3-e.c. is the unique Boolean-order-eight example. Chromatic-number research on Latin-square graphs and general pebble-game theory do not entail this classification. Previously published related claims handle 2-e.c. deletion resilience or different incidence languages, not 3-e.c. over arbitrary Latin squares. No dominating exact theorem was located; inaccessible full texts and possible alternate names are openly recorded as priority risks.
residual_risks: Historical priority is not proven by unsuccessful keyword or semantic searches. Another characterization of three-direction 3-e.c. net graphs may exist under different terminology.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural classification, not a chosen small-parameter curiosity: three-point extension rigidity forces any Latin-square table to be isotopic to a Boolean group and then eliminates every rank except three. The precise finite survivor gives a unique 64-vertex FO^4 model of the random-graph theory within a classical broad family, and its vertex-critical nature is structurally explained. It identifies a barrier to extending classical affine-plane constructions with only three directions. Neither correctness nor code is treated as sufficient for value; the algebraic obstruction and sharp classification supply the substantive motivation.
